messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Gabapentin is a prescription medicine.
Gabapentin is used to treat partial seizures.
Gabapentin is used to treat nerve pain from shingles.
Gabapentin is used to treat restless legs syndrome.
The restless legs syndrome treatment is for the Horizant brand only.
Gabapentin may also be prescribed off-label for other conditions.
These conditions include diabetic nerve pain, anxiety, and fibromyalgia.
Gabapentin is thought to work by calming overactive nerve signals in the brain and nervous system.
Gabapentin is an anticonvulsant and nerve pain medication from the drug class gabapentinoids
Gabapentin brand names are Neurontin, Gralise, Horizant, and Relgaabi.
These brand names may not be interchangeable.
Gabapentin is not a federally controlled substance.
Some states classify Gabapentin as Schedule V.
Other states require gabapentin prescriptions to be reported to their prescription drug monitoring program.
This program is known as the PDMP.
Rules on refills and quantity limits vary by state.
The most common side effects of gabapentin are dizziness.
They include drowsiness (somnolence).
Triples: [["Gabapentin", "is a", "prescription medicine"], ["Gabapentin", "treats", "partial seizures"], ["Gabapentin", "treats", "nerve pain from shingles"], ["Gabapentin", "treats", "restless legs syndrome"], ["restless legs syndrome treatment", "is for", "Horizant brand only"], ["Gabapentin", "may be prescribed off label for", "other conditions"], ["other conditions", "include", "diabetic nerve pain"], ["other conditions", "include", "anxiety"], ["other conditions", "include", "fibromyalgia"], ["Gabapentin", "has mechanism of action", "calming overactive nerve signals in the brain and nervous system"], ["Gabapentin", "belongs to drug class", "gabapentinoids"], ["Gabapentin", "has brand name", "Neurontin"], ["Gabapentin", "has brand name", "Gralise"], ["Gabapentin", "has brand name", "Horizant"], ["Gabapentin", "has brand name", "Relgaabi"], ["brand names", "may not be", "interchangeable"], ["Gabapentin", "is not a", "federally controlled substance"], ["Gabapentin", "classified as", "Schedule V"], ["Gabapentin", "requires prescriptions to be reported to", "prescription drug monitoring program"], ["prescription drug monitoring program", "is known as", "PDMP"], ["rules on refills and quantity limits", "vary by", "state"], ["Gabapentin", "has side effect", "dizziness"], ["Gabapentin", "has side effect", "drowsiness (somnolence)"]]
Relations: ["belongs to drug class", "classified as", "has brand name", "has mechanism of action", "has side effect", "include", "is a", "is for", "is known as", "is not a", "may be prescribed off label for", "may not be", "requires prescriptions to be reported to", "treats", "vary by"]
Answer:

completion:
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.  
classified as: The subject drug is classified under the regulatory category specified by the object entity.  
has brand name: The subject drug is marketed under the brand name specified by the object entity.  
has mechanism of action: The subject drug functions by the mechanism described in the object entity.  
has side effect: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect specified by the object entity.  
include: The object entity is an example or member of the subject entity.  
is a: The subject entity is categorized as the object entity.  
is for: The subject entity is specifically applicable or relevant to the object entity.  
is known as: The object entity is the commonly recognized name for the subject entity.  
is not a: The subject entity is explicitly not categorized as the object entity.  
may be prescribed off label for: The subject drug may be used for the condition specified by the object entity despite not being officially approved for it.  
may not be: The subject entity is not interchangeable with the object entity.  
requires prescriptions to be reported to: The subject entity mandates that prescriptions for the drug be reported to the object entity.  
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
vary by: The subject entity differs depending on the object entity.
